b: Seal one pair of your piles that adds up to exactly 7, and another pair that adds up to exactly 11.
Do both and the duel is yours.
Suns and Blooms add. Moons and Thorns subtract.
Only the top card of a pile counts. Cards beneath are hidden — even from you.
The four 13s are Forces: Flare, Overgrowth, Eclipse and Bramble. They have no value.
You hold 4 cards. Cast every one, onto any pile — yours or your opponent's.
Each card goes on top of a pile and covers whatever was showing. Play as many cards as you like on one pile.
Then end your turn and draw back up to 4.
A Force covering a pile blasts it away — every card in it goes to the Spent pile.
A Force you cover with another card is hidden and does nothing... until that pile is blasted later.
A Force may start an empty pile, but it can't be left on top when your turn ends.
Whenever two of your piles add to 7 or 11, tap Seals to lock them. An empty pile counts as 0.
On your own turn you can lock and unlock as often as you like. Unlocking frees your piles so you can play on them again.
You win if both the 7 and the 11 are locked when your turn ends.

Opening player: if you opened the round and seal both, your opponent gets one last turn. If they seal both too, it is a draw. If a Force breaks one of your seals, your win is cancelled and play goes on.
Locked piles are frozen — except to a Force, which can shatter one and free its partner.
Never end a turn with an empty pile of your own, unless it is locked.
A duel is played over several rounds, as a race to 7 or 11 points. Pick which on the menu.
Seal both targets to win a round for 2 points. If both players seal out, each takes 2. If the deck runs dry, the player who is closer wins it for 1. A deck-out draw scores nothing.
Lose a round while still holding one seal and you take 1 point anyway.
If both players pass the target in the same round, the higher total wins. If you are level, play on until someone leads.
You choose who opens the first round. After that the opener switches every round.
